subject: Access runbook + service-account signoff for FinSecure onboarding
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Access runbook + service-account signoff for FinSecure onboarding

Alex,

Attaching the first draft of the access-control runbook for the FinSecure onboarding. High level asks below so we can lock the technical cutover window.

Attachments: access-runbook-draft.pdf, service-account-matrix.csv

Key items we need confirmed from your side:
- SSO / SAML: Please confirm the EntityID and ACS endpoints you'll expose for the Redwood app (we included placeholders in the runbook). Also confirm required assertions (email, name, groups).
- SCIM: We proposed scim v2 with attributes: userName, givenName, familyName, active, groups. Confirm if FinSecure requires custom attributes (employeeId, department).
- IP allowlists: We listed the recommended egress CIDR ranges for your firewall (section 3.2). Can you confirm whether you need per-application IPs or a single org-level allowlist?
- Service accounts: The attached CSV lists recommended service-account names and minimal scopes. We need signoff on names and whether any of these must be rotated via your KMS/HSM procedures.
- Org policies: Any stricter retention flags or session timeout policies we should apply during the pilot?

Proposed next steps and timeline:
1) Confirm SAML metadata + SCIM attribute mappings by 2028-04-05.
2) Exchange test SAML metadata and start SCIM provisioning in our staging environment 2028-04-08 to 2028-04-12.
3) Schedule a technical call (30–45m) the week of 2028-04-10 to validate ACS/SCIM and IP rules.

If you prefer, Marissa can run the coordination and provide an editable certification worksheet for your security team to sign.

Thanks,

Rafael Mendes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: access-runbook-draft.pdf (12 pages, outlines SAML/SCIM/IP/service-account plan), service-account-matrix.csv (mapping of internal roles to required scopes)

From: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@finsecure.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access runbook + service-account signoff for FinSecure onboarding

Rafael,

Thanks for the runbook — quick read-through and a few clarifications from security: 

- SCIM attributes: We need employeeId and department in SCIM (both required). Can Redwood map those to our internal ldapUid and deptCode?
- IP allowlist: We prefer per-application IPs if feasible; our perimeter team is reluctant to open org-wide ranges. If per-app is not possible, we need the CIDR ranges to be routed to a dedicated proxy cluster.
- Service accounts: Will the service-account keys be accessible to our SecOps team, or does Redwood hold the private keys? We prefer a shared rotation policy (we use HashiCorp Vault).

Also looping in security@finsecure.com for the formal signoff and to coordinate firewall change windows.

On the tech call, can we aim for 2028-04-11 in the morning (ET)?

Regards,
Alex Barnes
Director, Platform Security
FinSecure
security@finsecure.com

Rafael / team,

Quick validation notes from implementation: 
- SAML: We can support their requested EntityID/ACS values. I need the test IdP metadata (cert + entityID). Recommend we ask them to provide a signed SAML response for staging.
- SCIM: We support employeeId and department mapping out-of-the-box; will add ldapUid -> employeeId and deptCode -> department mappings to the staging connector config. I'll push the mapping to staging once they confirm exact attribute names.
- IP allowlist: Per-app IPs are possible but require dedicated egress on our side (we'll advertise a different NAT pool per tenant app). That requires an infra ticket and ~5 business days lead time to provision. If FinSecure wants immediate staging, proxy routing is faster (1–2 days) but production per-app requires scheduling.
- Service accounts: We don't hold customer private keys. We can integrate with HashiCorp Vault for rotation. Need a short Ops doc from FinSecure on their rotation policies (rotation window, access groups).

I'll add these as checklist items and propose the infra ticket now (ONB-4521). Recommend we schedule the tech call with engineering leads: Ben Carter (me), Diego (network eng), and Monica for policy.

Ben Carter
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for looping in your security mailbox. Per internal validation:

- SCIM: We can include employeeId and department. Ben will add ldapUid -> employeeId and deptCode -> department mappings in staging; please confirm exact attribute names/format.
- IP allowlist: We can do per-app egress but need 5 business days for infra provisioning. For the staging window we can put you on proxy routing.
- Service accounts: Redwood will not retain customer private keys. We support integration with HashiCorp Vault for rotation; please share your rotation policy doc.

Next steps:
- Please confirm SCIM attribute names by 2028-04-05.
- Tech call: proposing Tue, 2028-04-11 at 10:00 AM ET (30–45m). If that doesn't work, we'll propose additional slots. 
- I'll share an editable certification worksheet by EOD that your security team can sign and return.
